But the U.S. has been engaged in smaller-scale strikes against Iran for several weeks, officials said. Some of the officials described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, report Alexander Ward, Lara Seligman and Shelby Holliday.

Control of Congress Is on the Line as America Heads to the Polls
 
Plus, the U.S. strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island, and higher prices might not save Apple’s slowing growth machine
 
 
CHIQUI ESTEBAN
 

1. FROM MY DESK

 

Election Day is here. President Trump and Republicans are vying to maintain their coveted “trifecta”—control of the House, Senate and presidency, while Democrats are aiming to gain a majority in both chambers. Democrats are favored to win a majority in the House. The picture is hazier in the Senate, where the majority will be decided by several high-profile races in states such as Texas, Michigan and Alaska.

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here. If you’re reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

 
 
 

2. TODAY’S HEADLINES

 

• The midterms will offer clues to just how much change can come from a new Congress and what likely will be the most wide-open presidential primary elections in years.

 

• Trump’s election-eve speech, which some White House officials pitched as a capstone to a flurry of rallies, centered on the many construction projects and renovations the president has overseen during his second term.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

 

The U.S. strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as Trump talks down war risks.

 

The attack is the latest of a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks as Trump touted the possibility of a diplomatic deal. The assault follows comments by Trump playing down the possibility of a return to war with Iran after today’s elections. But the U.S. has been engaged in smaller-scale strikes against Iran for several weeks, officials said. Some of the officials described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, report Alexander Ward, Lara Seligman and Shelby Holliday.

 

5.

 

These associates had a golden ticket to Big Law—until Weil Gotshal collapsed.

 

Throughout October, second-year law student Madeleine Edwards received a series of upbeat emails from Weil Gotshal & Manges, where she had landed a coveted job for next summer. A very different message landed on Oct. 29, the day after the law firm announced it was dissolving: Weil’s recruiters said it would no longer be able to honor the 2027 job offers. The demise of a large and respected law firm virtually overnight is without precedent and is sending shock waves through the legal job market, report Mariah Timms, Jasmine Li and Lindsay Ellis. Weil’s roughly 600 associates, as well as law students with future job offers, are likely to be the hardest hit.

8. THE NUMBER

 
$1.5 trillion
 

The initial public offering valuation (around $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion) institutional investors are urging Anthropic to target later this month, according to people familiar with the matter, well below figures closer to $2 trillion that had been bandied about. Prospective buyers of the Claude maker’s shares cite a list of concerning factors including choppy markets and growing concerns about overexposure to AI bets.

 
 
 

9. AND FINALLY…

 

40-somethings are having a really hard time admitting they can no longer see.

 

Presbyopia is the natural change of the lens in your eye as you age, resulting in a harder time seeing things up close. Despite a rite of passage as old as humankind, vision changes still come as news to many—and it’s especially hard on a generation of people who have actively embraced the idea that your 40s might be the new 30s. They’re not afraid of Botox, GLPs and Pilates. What does scare them: admitting they have a problem when the waiter brings beet carpaccio after they swear they read beef.
